summary: Landlord must maintain the apartment in a habitable condition at all times. Any lease clause that waives this right is void and unenforceable.
Heat must be provided Oct 1 – May 31. Between 6am-10pm, min 68°F when outside is below 55°F. Between 10pm-6am, min 62°F always.
Security deposit cannot exceed ONE month's rent (for leases signed after June 14, 2019). Any clause requiring more is illegal.
Landlord must return security deposit (with itemized deduction list) within 14 days of move-out. Failure forfeits the right to make any deductions.
For tenants in place 1-2 years, landlord must give 60 days written notice of rent increase or non-renewal. 2+ years = 90 days notice.
Landlord must provide reasonable notice (typically 24 hours) before entering the apartment except in genuine emergencies. Lease clauses allowing entry without notice are unenforceable.
Landlord must give 14-day written notice for non-payment, 10-day notice for lease violations, 30-day notice for month-to-month non-renewal.
Late fees cannot exceed $50 or 5% of monthly rent (whichever is less), and cannot be charged until rent is 5+ days late.
In NYC buildings with 3+ units, if a tenant openly keeps a pet for 3+ months with the landlord's knowledge, the landlord loses the right to evict over a no-pets clause (Pet Law).

It is illegal for NYC landlords to refuse to rent or set different terms based on lawful source of income (including housing vouchers/Section 8). Any lease clause making vouchers a basis for denial is void.

Tenants in buildings with 4+ units have the right to sublet with landlord consent. Landlord cannot unreasonably withhold consent. Any lease clause prohibiting subletting entirely may be unenforceable.
Domestic violence survivors can terminate a lease early by giving written notice + documentation. No penalty. Any lease clause that prohibits this is void.
